newsitem.title: UK: Oil price rally pauses for breath, undertone firm.
newsitem.headline: Oil price rally pauses for breath, undertone firm.

text.p: A prolonged rally which took oil prices near post-Gulf War highs on Monday paused for breath on Tuesday but short-term sentiment remained bullish on weather-driven demand.
In London, February futures for benchmark Brent crude ended the day at $24.58 a barrel, up two cents from Monday's close.

Despite the early declines, which traders attributed to light profit-taking after Monday's 45-cent gains, Brent is not far from the $25.06 post Gulf War peak it hit in mid-October, its highest since 1991.
Forecasts for continued frigid temperatures in Europe and the United States, the world's largest heating oil consumers, will keep the heat under the rally, traders said.
"We're looking firm because it is a weather-driven season and it's cold here and cold in the United States," said Peter Gignoux, head of the London energy desk at Smith, Barney.
Traders are looking forward to weekly data from the American Petroleum Institute later Tuesday on weekly U.S. oil inventory shifts to gauge demand.

Brokers GNI said in its daily energy market report that early forecasts for the API report are not very bullish and may show a build in heating oil stocks reflecting unseasonably high temperatures in some parts of the United States last week.
But they see no reason for a big selloff unless the statistics were "very bearish."
"Unless the stats are very bearish, the complex still looks quite positive from a fundamental perspective this week," GNI said.
Low stocks of heating oil have kept the fire stoked under a prolonged oil price rally which began in the second half of 1996 and stunned most oil pundits who had predicted much lower prices.
The price of the OPEC basket of seven crudes the cartel uses as a reference averaged $20.29 in 1996, OPEC said on Tuesday, well above the 1995 average of $16.86.
